subject: Release timing, enablement & exception plan — staggered rollout for Runtime V2
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Patel <devon@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Release timing, enablement & exception plan — staggered rollout for Runtime V2

Team —

We need to lock the operational plan for the Runtime V2 release targeted for the week of Apr 25. The ask is to land a staggered rollout (canary -> region ramp -> full) because Acme (large enterprise pilot) requested a slower ramp and we have a couple of known exceptions (quantization vs. certain older GPU drivers). High level items I need from each group by EOD Monday: 

- Product (David): explicit minimum feature set for Day-0 GA and prioritized exceptions that can be delayed.
- Eng (Markus): concrete timeline for the canary gates + estimated days needed for exception fixes.
- Ops (Jordan): blackout windows and suggested maintenance windows (avoid Eastern business hours if possible).
- CS/Enablement (Grace): enablement plan and customer-facing guidance for Acme (docs + playbook).
- Sales (Stephanie): any contractual notes/commitments made to Acme we should honor on timing/credits.

I attached a blank staggered-rollout-matrix for each of you to populate (matrix rows: region, model-variant, fallback model, gate criteria, rollback criteria, expected QPS). I will consolidate and circulate a final release checklist on Tuesday.

Attachments: [staggered-rollout-matrix.xlsx (13KB)] [release-notes-draft.md (4KB)]

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel
Program Manager, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Release timing, enablement & exception plan — staggered rollout for Runtime V2

Monica — thanks. Quick answers / clarifications from Product side: 

- Day-0 GA must include: streaming API parity with Runtime V1 (stream chunking and resumption), new batching controls (per-tenant max-batch-size), and model pinning API. Everything else can be staged post-GA.
- Exceptions we can tolerate for GA (but must have mitigations documented):
  * Quantized 4-bit weights on Ampere V1 drivers (falls back to FP16; slower but acceptable).
  * Model-variant A/B buckets for customers < 10k monthly tokens (we can delay A/B until after region ramp).

Questions for Eng: can we support per-tenant batch overrides in the canary? If not, that's a blocker for some enterprise customers and we should push that into pre-GA fixes.

Also tagging the Acme commitment: we said "no more than 2% downtime during ramp" in the proposal — Stephanie please confirm if that's still accurate.

-David
David Kim
Sr. Product Manager
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 13:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Release timing, enablement & exception plan — staggered rollout for Runtime V2

On Sun, Apr 11, 2027 at 11:12 AM David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Monica — thanks. Quick answers / clarifications from Product side: 

Short version from Eng: 

- Per-tenant batch overrides: we can ship a minimal per-tenant throttle in the canary (config flag + soft limit) but the full enforcement path (kernel-level guardrails) will land post-GA (2 weeks). Recommend we document the soft-limit behavior in the playbook.
- Quantization on older Ampere drivers: root cause is a driver vectorization bug on customer images. Our options:
  1) Advise fallback to FP16 (works today)
  2) Push a small runtime shim that detects driver version and forces fallback (low-risk) — ETA 3 business days if we prioritize.

- Canary gates I propose:
  * Gate 1 (internal canary): synthetic workload smoke tests + KV cache sanity (Day 0 of canary)
  * Gate 2 (acme pilot group): small customer traffic (5% of target QPS) with expanded tracing
  * Gate 3 (regional ramp): incremental region enablement with automated rollback on 5xx > 0.5% or latency p95 > 300ms

I will populate the matrix with specific timelines and will flag the driver-shim as an "accelerate" item.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Release timing, enablement & exception plan — staggered rollout for Runtime V2

Folks —

Ops constraints and propose windows: 

- Suggested canary start: Tue Apr 27 00:00 UTC to allow late-day deploys in us-west after business hours.
- Avoid maintenance in these windows for east-coast customers: 13:00-18:00 EDT (we should plan rolling maintenance 22:00-02:00 UTC).
- Blackout for Acme escalations: during their weekly biz-review (Wednesdays 14:00-15:00 EDT) — flagging so CS doesn't schedule demos then.

On rollback automation: we will enforce automatic rollback on threshold breaches; need a final list of the thresholds (Markus proposed 5xx > 0.5% and p95 > 300ms). Also need explicit list of regions that must be excluded from immediate rollback (e.g., test/regional perf experiments).

Jordan
Jordan Blake
SRE Manager, Service Reliability

Thanks — Grace here with the enablement plan summary: 

- Customer playbook draft (attached in Google Doc, link below) covers: expected behavior, known exceptions (quantization fallback), how to interpret rollout statuses, and how to request exemptions.
- Training: I can run two 45-min live sessions for CS/Support on Apr 28 and Apr 29 UTC-friendly times. Recording + quick FAQ will be posted to the Enablement space.
- External-facing release notes: keep the first note explicit about the GA feature subset and list the driver/quantization exception with the recommended fallback steps (we should not bury this in fine print).

Grace
